chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who had a right (debt) upon another man, and he had assigned it to his young children from his dependents. The debtor mentioned to the creditor that the money was upon him. He said to him, 'There is no difficulty for you in it in this world or in the Hereafter.' I asked, 'Is it permissible for him to take back what he assigned from it, even though he had assigned it to them?' He said, 'Yes, it is permissible, but it will be that he gave it to them and then took it back from them and assigned it to you.'
ai.seo_question: Can a debtor reclaim a debt he previously assigned to his children?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the validity of a debtor assigning his receivables to his minor children is affirmed, yet he retains the prerogative to revoke this assignment and reclaim the funds. This highlights the flexibility in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding the revocability of such assignments, ensuring the debtor’s financial control without spiritual or worldly penalty. The narration underscores the practical balance between familial provision and debt recovery in Islamic law.
